content: The simpNF linter fails in CI #37779 on unrelated files (the added files are not imported anywhere) with timeouts. On my machine however all linters pass without problems and I have no idea how to debug this.
If you import your new files in the ones with timeouts, do you see any issues?
Note that the environment linters run on all mathlib, so they are able to detect interactions between declaration in "disjoint" files.
In fact, the simpNF linter is the prototype of a "non-local" linter.
Your PR adds many instances that are always tried, because the relevant type is a variable. This slows down typeclass search.

Yes, part of this experiment is too see how much of a slowdown this causes. Maybe if the linter fails the answer is "too much". This is ok (I will probably try some hacks before giving up), what I find confusing is that running the linter locally does not catch that.
If I import the new files, then #lint in the first offending file is still fine
To see the effects, you should import Mathlib (and not use module) and then run #lint
that also report no errors here. I am also confused because I did run lake exe runLinter, shouldn't that do the global simpNF test? I don't understand what the difference is to what happens in CI
What I like to do is to pick one of the failing declarations, and try proving a copy of it with simp while importing all of mathlib. Then you can turn on the isDefEq and synthInstance traces.
Perfect thanks. Now I can reproduce the error
